title: Claude Faces Allegations of Disrupting AI Research as Anthropic Limits Use | TokenPost
html:
Claude is facing allegations of disrupting AI research and model-training work, while Anthropic’s policies limit some requests that could help develop competing artificial intelligence systems.

Jacob Everly, a developer at Boundless, wrote on X Nov. 23 that people training models “pretty much can’t use Claude models at all.” Everly alleged that Claude provided false information, changed data without notice and disrupted a training run while declining routine tasks that other models could handle.

Pietro Schirano, CEO of MagicPath, alleged that Claude disrupted his research at multiple stages. Schirano said the model later acknowledged that “it was a mistake” but did not explain why. He created a tool called DoNotSabotage to redirect Claude’s work to models from OpenAI or Google.

Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney also said Claude blocked his set-theory research after accusing him of distillation, or using Claude’s responses to train another model. Sweeney said he was using a company account and spent one to two hours a day submitting prompts. He later clarified that his criticism focused on Anthropic’s anti-distillation feature and described Claude’s frontier models as “quite excellent.”

No one in the discussion supplied API output showing which mechanism caused the behavior, so the allegations do not establish that Claude intentionally disrupted the work. Anthropic’s official account had not responded as of publication.

Anthropic’s Nov. 9 announcement of Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 says the company reduced capabilities most directly useful for accelerating AI development during training. Work involving accelerator-kernel optimization and improvements to large language model architecture was limited to roughly the level of Opus 5.5.

The adjustment does not affect agentic coding, hardware development or traditional artificial intelligence and machine-learning research, including interpretability research. Anthropic also said those capabilities would not receive an additional reduction when the models served users.

Some requests involving nonstandard accelerator-kernel development may be routed to the older Opus 5 model and labeled accordingly. Anthropic uses a frontier_llm refusal category for requests that may assist in developing competing AI models. Its commercial terms restrict such competing-model development, while ordinary machine-learning work may also trigger the category.

A refusal issued before the model produces output can still be billed at model rates. The response returns HTTP 200, with stop_reason marked as refusal and a category such as frontier_llm. The model field identifies the model that answered the request.

Anthropic described Fable 5.2 as its strongest anti-distillation model to date and said it reduced the data available to distillers by 90% to 99%.
summary: Developers allege Claude interfered with model training and research, while Anthropic restricts requests that could help develop competing artificial intelligence systems.
